announced that its Ship Repair business won a $115.66M U.S. Navy contract for fitting out and post-shakedown availability work on amphibious transport dock ships LPD-30 and LPD-31.
The contract includes options that could increase its cumulative value to $527.53M if fully exercised.
The work will be performed in San Diego, California, and is expected to be completed by December 2028.
However, if all options are exercised, work could continue through May 2031.

The U.S. Navy will initially obligate $7.82M in shipbuilding and conversion funds, including $7.49M from fiscal 2026 and $327.89K from fiscal 2025. The funds will not expire at the end of the current fiscal year.
Naval Sea Systems Command is the contracting activity.

title: BAE Systems wins $116M contract for amphibious navy ships work
